Arthritis Kids

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
Children suffering from the debilitating and in some cases terminal side effects of auto immune disease, are being left to suffer, while medical aids try and deny them their right to biologics. But one mom, Catherine McCormack, has made it her mission to fight this fight. She has taken on over 40 cases, where medical aids have tried to deny these families biologics even though they fall under PMB care for Arthritis, and WON
“These cases take months, months where these kids are in horrific pain or permanently disfigured due to being unmedicated. It is criminal”

This isn’t one or two cases, it is a systemic issue that the CMS has committed to tackling with all medical aids, but it is (as usual) taking forever to take any real action.

Further information:
Case study 1
Jennifer 14-years-old
On and off illness for two years
Doctors thought it was the appendix, so it was removed. But she didn't get better
Diagnosed Crohns disease, which has caused JIA (Juvenile idiopathic Arthritis)
She needed biologics immediately to put her immune system to sleep, so they could get the inflammation under control. Discovery rejected their application
They applied for Ex gratia, which was granted, but has expired and their stock is finished next week. Catherine has taken on the case and will lodge a complaint with the CMS.
Their first claim should never have been rejected.

If she goes off the medication she will relapse and land up back in hospital
Next option is bowl removal.

Case 2
Skyla 9-years-old
She contracted covid and started getting random rashes and high temperatures
In and out of hospital for months, very sick
Hospital for a month, lymph nodes removed. No diagnoses
Eventually JIA was diagnosed
December 2022, while in hospital discovery agreed to pay for Biologics for one months and then her doctors had to motivate for a continuation. They then rejected the claim for a continuation, mom had to raise R8400 for January supply, her last injection is next week
Reality is that she is suffering long term damage from the cortisones that she is on, her bon density is extremely low and her hips have begun to degenerate. Without the biologic she will land up in hospital again, she can't live a healthy normal life without it.

Long term side effects for these kids if they go untreated:
Blindness
permanent disfigurement - one arm may be long, bones that grow in the wrong direction
Excruciating pain

ARTHRITIS SCRIPT FOR VIEWING

SKYLA AND BONGS PAINTING SCENE – don’t strap Skyla here
B: what you making
S:Im making me
B:what's the toughest thing about being sick
B:it's hard
S:why
Because I can't do anything that my brothers do.
B:What happens when you do?
S:Then I get really tired, and then my chest gets tight.

CYNTHIA
00:00:32:08 - 00:01:01:11
we started noticing a rash all over her body and fevers, persistent fevers. Nothing would break the fever.
She had all sorts of tests done. They couldn't find anything.

00:13:07:01 - 00:13:08:02
Speaker 1
Do you pray sometimes?
00:13:08:07 - 00:13:08:17
Speaker 3
Yes.
“I pray i get better every day”

Catherine: And then THEY said, okay, she's got juvenile arthritis.


3” music Skyla in bed – slow down

VO 1: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis, or JIA, is a chronic auto-immune disease in children under sixteen. For reasons not properly understood, the child’s protective immune system attacks and kills healthy cells causing excruciating joint pain. For 9-year-old Skyla Stewart, it’s been life-altering.

The bear – upsound – subtitle it italics ?

Black open like a video starting – with audio
Ella verite beat – “Hello.. and she is off”

VO2: Like Skyla, Ella McCormick suffered the debilitating effects of Juvenile Arthritis. Her mom, Catherine, felt helpless.

Catherine interview
the pain was SO extreme that ella couldn't even stand to be dressed or covered in a duvet

CATHERINE
I remember sitting in a paediatrician’s rooms and I asked if she was in pain and the paediatrician said that she was in more pain than I could imagine. And it was that that just undid me completely. We had tried to sleeptrain at one point. And the idea that we were forcing her to sleep through pain took me a long time to forgive myself for.

Video of ella on the bike beat

VO 3: But there is a way out of this pain and anxiety: cutting edge pharmaceutical treatments known as biologics. They contain living cells that target and deactivate the area of the immune system causing the inflammation. Free of pain it means children can be children again. But there’s a catch: these drugs are expensive.

2” of video of ella

VO 4: Fortunately, Catherine McCormick’s family is on a top tier medical plan. So, when Ella stopped responding to all other treatments, biologics were immediately approved. Within 18 months it was as if the arthritis had never happened.

CATHERINE
The child that emerged without pain was completely different to the child that we'd come to know in pain. And it was like we'd met her for the first time.

Ella video

VO5. Skyla wasn’t that lucky. Her doctors, urgently trying to ease her suffering, recommended a biologic called Actemera. But her mother, Cynthia, says when they requested permission for the drug from their provider, MediHelp, they were told their plan didn’t cover the cost.

cynthia and bongs
How does it sit with you that from the medical aids, it's almost like you have to be rich enough to be. Well.
It's traumatizing. And as a parent, you feel helpless

VO 6: Without the right medication Skyla’s condition inevitably deteriorated. She was in excruciating pain and eventually had to be hospitalised. Her medical team now had no choice but to administer the biologic.

cynthia
It worked. She got better. And then they said, okay, so now we are going to approach the medical aid and say, okay, she has no choice but to have the actemra biological injection

VO7: Then in January this year, a small breakthrough: Medihelp finally agreed to pay for a biologic which costs 8400 rand a month. But the good news was tempered with yet more frustration: because the Stewarts were on a limited plan, costs would only be covered for one month.

Cynthia, what happens if Skyla doesn't get this biologic?
She could have total organ failure. So because their immune system fights itself, it fights everything in the body, the cells, the red blood cells, the kidneys, the liver attacks everything.

VO8: A terrifying prospect. And shockingly one that Skyla and her parents shouldn’t have had to confront. That’s because medical aids – all of them – are legally obligated to fund the diagnosis and treatment of Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis and cover all care costs, if certain requirements and protocols are met, because as it turns out JIA is a so-called Prescribed Minimum Benefit.

00:57:21:24 - 00:57:49:04
Speaker 3
And the regulations that that we're talking about here are incredibly clear.
00:57:49:13 - 00:58:02:18
Speaker 3
for people who are part of a medical scheme, who have a pub condition or chronic disease and who meet the criteria of the regulations that would fund them, it's very simple.

VO9: Having seen the impact of biologics on her daughter, Catherine is fighting for those denied their benefit. She’s now the Executive Director of Arthritis South Africa, a campaigner taking on big business on behalf of children with JIA.

UPS FROM PHONE CALL HERE.00:00:38:15 - 00:01:05:10
So I just wanted to touch bases on where we at at the moment.

VO10: Catherine is adamant Skyla qualified for a Biologic from her family’s VERY FIRST application to Medihelp, based on Prescribed Minimum Benefit regulations.

CATHERINE AND CYNTHIA PHONE CALL:
Just so you say she has it on a weekly basis?
00:01:11:11 - 00:01:12:17
Speaker 1
Yes, weekly basis.
00:01:13:06 - 00:01:15:16
Speaker 2
Okay. So actually, from next week you point out to that, right?
00:01:15:18 - 00:01:17:13
Speaker 1
That's correct.

VO11. But Skyla’s isn’t the only case Catherine is fighting. Every week, more families are asking for help.

Jennifer
I did ballet for about 11 years and I just went on to points. But I couldn't anymore because I was so tired and I was nauseous and sick all the time.
That broke me.

VO 12: Jennifer Carstens was dealt a cruel blow by JIA. Diagnosed in January last year, along with Crohn’s Disease which affects the bowel, her doctors immediately requested the biologic, Humira, in a bid to save her life.

karin jennas mom
Discovery's response to me was upgrade your plan or we can't help you guys.

VO11: Discovery maintained that Biologics are not a PMB level of care, even though the council for medical schemes has repeatedly ruled that they are,
and referred Jennifer’s mom Karin to ex-gratia, which is basically a charitable fund for members who can’t afford medication.
Even then, the medical aid is not obliged to pay. (PAUSE)

However, Discovery Health relented… for 6 months.

jennifer
Since going on the injections? I feel like I got myself back.
My personality. Back when I was not on medications, I really felt like I was losing myself.

karin jens mom
The medication gave my daughter back to me, gave her life back…
tick tock scene up sound

VO 12: the smiles, the dance moves hide a sad reality ... today is Jennifer’s last injection…

KARIN JENNS MOM
If Jennifer doesn't get this injection she's going to be ten times worse than she was in Jan. As soon as that slip up comes back without medication there is going to be more complications

VO 12: So, as Jennifers mother Karin readies for another struggle, whose job is it to ensure medical aids follow the law and provide the treatments necessary to ease these children’s suffering? In late 2021 Catherine took her concerns to the Council for Medical Schemes or CMS, the official regulator able to get service providers to stop this apparent abuse of power.

CATHERINE
I'm not asking for the CMS to order the medical schemes to fund these treatments where they're not appropriate or where they don't meet the criteria of the regulations.
I just want the CMS to tell medical schemes that they have to take the law into account

VO 13: The CMS acknowledged Catherine’s concerns and met with the schemes in question. But, since then… nothing.

CATHERINE
It's been six months and I had an update from the CMS. I have no indication that it's progressing at all.

NEW VO: We asked the CMS for an interview, but they declined.

VO 14: Meanwhile, as they await a response from Medihelp, Skyla is getting her last injection, too. Her family is now relying on donations to cover next month’s supply.

CYNTHIA - SKYLAS MOM
We are sort of at an end of the road type of thing. We, we, we don't know what to do.

VO 13: Catherine took the Stewart’s plight to the CMS, lodging an official complaint against Medihelp. Then, something unexpected happened.

We sent MediHelp an interview request. They refused, but two days later informed us Skyler's medication would, in fact, be funded. Except they didn't tell her parents, nor Catherine, who had to hear it from us.

VO 14: Despite the coincidence, Medihelp say their decision had nothing to do with our request. But, whatever the reason, Skyla is finally on the right medication and - given time – could be back playing netballl with her brothers.


VO 15:
After claiming the biologic, Humira, doesn’t fall within the standard level of Prescribed Minimum Benefit care for JIA, Discovery Health approved a year’s supply of the drug to Jennifer from their Chronic Fund. It came within days of Catherines enquiries about the case. But when we asked why it was suddenly being approved and not sent to Ex-gratia, Discovery backtracked, alleging there was a mistake in communication and the biologic was been approved for year on ex-gratia and not from the chronic fund

Catherine How many cases have you had to fight for?
so far I've done 40,
40 in the last year and a half.
And how many of you won?
All of them
What?
Haven't lost any cases.

NEW VO: But while each victory has been life-changing, not one of those 40 fights should have been necessary.

metadata.Summary: Children suffering from the debilitating and in some cases terminal side effects of auto immune disease, are being left to suffer, while medical aids try and deny them their right to biologics. But one mom, Catherine McCormack, has made it her mission to fight this fight. She has taken on over 40 cases, where medical aids have tried to deny these families biologics even though they fall under PMB care for Arthritis, and WON “These cases take months, months where these kids are in horrific pain or permanently disfigured due to being unmedicated. It is criminal” This isn’t one or two cases, it is a systemic issue that the CMS has committed to tackling with all medical aids, but it is (as usual) taking forever to take any real action.
metadata.Further information: Case study 1 Jennifer 14-years-old On and off illness for two years Doctors thought it was the appendix, so it was removed. But she didn't get better Diagnosed Crohns disease, which has caused JIA (Juvenile idiopathic Arthritis) She needed biologics immediately to put her immune system to sleep, so they could get the inflammation under control. Discovery rejected their application They applied for Ex gratia, which was granted, but has expired and their stock is finished next week. Catherine has taken on the case and will lodge a complaint with the CMS. Their first claim should never have been rejected. If she goes off the medication she will relapse and land up back in hospital Next option is bowl removal. Case 2 Skyla 9-years-old She contracted covid and started getting random rashes and high temperatures In and out of hospital for months, very sick Hospital for a month, lymph nodes removed. No diagnoses Eventually JIA was diagnosed December 2022, while in hospital discovery agreed to pay for Biologics for one months and then her doctors had to motivate for a continuation. They then rejected the claim for a continuation, mom had to raise R8400 for January supply, her last injection is next week Reality is that she is suffering long term damage from the cortisones that she is on, her bon density is extremely low and her hips have begun to degenerate. Without the biologic she will land up in hospital again, she can't live a healthy normal life without it. Long term side effects for these kids if they go untreated: Blindness permanent disfigurement - one arm may be long, bones that grow in the wrong direction Excruciating pain
